mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a recession.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism does not activate during a confirmed recession.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 5.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual tightening and inflationary shock, which increases both interest rates and input costs, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 12-month moving average
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 55% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent increase in both real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) and retail sales (proxied by RSAFS) above their 6-month moving averages signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and RSAFS both exceed 6-month moving average
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the unemployment rate below 4% for four consecutive months signals an overheating labor market, which precedes tighter monetary policy and higher wage inflation, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related equities and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month moving average for 6 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 55% of triggered episodes.
